chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them both), that he said: Ali (Allah's blessings be upon him) said:
Do not say: 'Ramadhan', however, say: 'the Month of Ramadhan', for indeed, you do not know what Ramadhan is.

key_terms.مَا رَمَضَانُ: What Ramadhan is (referring to its true essence/status)

ai.seo_question: Why should one say 'the Month of Ramadhan' instead of just 'Ramadhan'?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and reverence in speech, distinguishing between the proper noun 'Ramadhan' and the descriptive phrase 'the Month of Ramadhan.' This linguistic nuance reflects the theological concept that the divine reality of the month transcends its mere label, urging believers to acknowledge the limits of their comprehension regarding its spiritual depth. It serves as a reminder that true reverence involves recognizing the sanctity that exceeds human definition.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, and Muhammed bin Hussain, from Muhammed bin Yahya al-Khath’ami, from Ghiyath bin Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon them both, that he said: Ali, Allah’s blessings be upon him, said:
Do not say: «Ramadhan», however, say: «the Month of Ramadhan», for indeed, you do not know what Ramadhan is.
